intro: A photo is often faster than typing. Point at a plate or a packaged food, review what Buddy recognises, then choose where it should go.
buddyTip: Live camera has Auto · Tap chips for barcodes and QR. Auto freezes when a code is recognized; Tap waits for your shutter. Shopping defaults Auto; Home meal camera defaults Tap. Plates always need the shutter.
mission: Log one plated meal from the Home camera (shutter). Scan one packaged food — try Auto once, then Tap if you prefer control — and send it to exactly one place: Foodiary, Quick Food, Stock, or the shopping list.
why: Complex plates are hard to type. A picture gives Buddy something concrete to estimate while you keep eating or parenting or commuting.
Packaged foods already have an identity. One scan should be enough to eat, remember, stock, or buy — without hunting through four screens.
Camera logging still requires human judgment. Recognition can miss sauces, oils, drinks beside the plate, or second helpings. Your confirmation protects honesty.
Gallery helps when you forgot to log in the moment but still have a photo — better than reconstructing from memory alone.
Mixed plates (buffets, shared tapas) need your portion story on confirm. The camera sees the table; you know your share.

points: Use camera or gallery on Home for plates — tap the shutter
Auto · Tap chips control barcode/QR snap (choice is remembered)
Shopping defaults Auto; meal camera defaults Tap — flip anytime on the live view
From Home with Tap, a barcode in frame + shutter still opens the pack card
Choose Eat (Foodiary), Remember (Quick Food), Have (Stock), or Buy (shopping list)
Plate photos stay eat + retake — a bowl is not a barcode
Confirm portions and missing fats/drinks before saving a meal
Edit later in Foodiary if you learn more

misconceptions.myth: The photo alone is perfect nutrition truth.
misconceptions.truth: Vision estimates help; portions and hidden fats still need you.

misconceptions.myth: Scanning a pack logs it as eaten.
misconceptions.truth: Nothing is written until you pick a destination. Eat, remember, have, and buy are different jobs.

misconceptions.myth: Blurry photos are fine — AI will figure it out.
misconceptions.truth: Clear plates produce better suggestions. Retake when you can.

how.lead: Make photo logging a tidy habit.
steps: Frame the full meal on Home and tap shutter — or open Shopping list camera for packs
Wait for the pack card, or capture before you destroy a plated meal
Pick one destination for a pack — or confirm Buddy’s plate draft
Add voice or text notes for oil, butter, dressings, beverages
Save; don’t double-log the same plate in Foodiary manually
how.buddyHelps: Buddy recognises the pack once, then the existing Foodiary, Quick Food, Stock, and shopping list do the work. For plates you remain editor-in-chief at confirm.

sections.title: Packaged foods
paras: Point at barcode bars, a product QR, or printed EAN / GTIN. Use Auto to snap when recognized, or Tap to freeze with the shutter. Buddy looks the pack up once and shows the same card. Then choose exactly one: Save to Foodiary (you ate it), Save as Quick Food (you eat it often — nothing logged today), Add to Stock (you have it), or Add to shopping list (you will buy it). Scan next keeps the camera up.
If Buddy does not know the pack, photograph the label or continue. Do not invent a food. Receipt photos still use the receipt flow — Add to Stock there is the same Stock ledger as a cupboard barcode.

sections.title: Labels and receipts
paras: Packaged foods and receipts can be clearer than plated meals. When Buddy reads a label, still check serving size versus what you ate.

sections.title: Privacy and sharing
paras: Avoid photographing other people’s faces or documents. Meal photos are for your coaching loop.

sections.title: When to prefer another mode
paras: Dark restaurants and tiny labels frustrate vision. Switch to voice: name the dish and a fair portion. The goal is a saved honest row, not a perfect photo.

mistakes.quote: I photographed the salad and ignored the dressing boat.
mistakes.why: Dressing may dominate energy. Log it explicitly.

mistakes.quote: I snapped after finishing and Buddy saw an empty plate.
mistakes.why: Capture before or describe leftovers. Empty crockery teaches little.

mistakes.quote: Recognition was wrong so I logged nothing.
mistakes.why: Edit the draft or switch to voice/text. The meal still counts.

mistakes.quote: I scanned a tin into Foodiary when I was unpacking shopping.
mistakes.why: Have ≠ eat. Use Add to Stock for the cupboard, Save to Foodiary when you open it.

encouragement: Point, recognise, choose. Camera logging exists to keep real life inside the right place — diary, shortcuts, cupboard, or list — not to pass a photography exam.
